home.metaDescription: Omah Pala sells nutmeg-fruit tea, syrup, and candy from Desa Wonokerto, made through the TOGA BERDAYA farmer program — export-ready, traceable to the plot.
home.heroCardTitle: Portrait of the TOGA BERDAYA program in Desa Wonokerto
home.introTitle1: Two problems that turn out to be
home.introBody: In Wonokerto, working-age adults are the group most affected by non-communicable disease. At the same time, nutmeg hasn’t been fully put to use. TOGA BERDAYA addresses both through one chain of work: from the field, to the production kitchen, to market.
home.pillarsTitle: Five pillars, each connected to the next.
home.productsTitle1: From the part that used to be
home.productsBody: Wonokerto's farmers use the nutmeg seed, then discard the fruit's flesh and skin. These products are made from that discarded part.
home.statsTitle: Targets you can check, not empty promises.
home.whyRow1Body: Every product carries a plot code and grower name you can trace on the Farms page.
home.whyRow2Title: The part that used to be wasted
home.whyRow2Body: The nutmeg fruit flesh, usually discarded, is now processed into a sellable product.
home.whyRow3Body: Every production stage is logged through the TOGA BERDAYA program, from seedling to packaging.
home.ecosystemTitle: The ecosystem map: from five pillars to real products and partners.
home.ecosystemBody: Click any node to see details about that pillar, product, or partner.

catalog.title: Processed products from TOGA Corner plants

catalog.introBody: Wonokerto villagers turn nutmeg and TOGA plants into food, beverages, and care products. Browse the selection below.
catalog.sectionPalaDesc: Wonokerto farmers use the nutmeg seed, then discard the fruit and skin. The products below are made from that discarded part.
catalog.sectionOtherPlantsDesc: Beyond nutmeg, Wonokerto residents grow a range of family medicinal (TOGA) plants in their home gardens. Products below are grouped by plant type to make browsing easier.

program.title: A five-month program built with residents
program.subtitle: TOGA BERDAYA is a PPK Ormawa HIMFA UII program combining non-communicable disease (NCD) prevention with cultivating TOGA (Tanaman Obat Keluarga — medicinal plants grown in home gardens) and economic empowerment for residents of Desa Wonokerto, Turi, Sleman.
program.metaDescription: TOGA BERDAYA: a five-month PPK Ormawa HIMFA UII program combining NCD prevention with TOGA cultivation and economic empowerment in Desa Wonokerto, Sleman.

polo.metaDescription: A QR scavenger hunt at the Omah Pala booth. Collect stamps and redeem rewards.
polo.title: Find your Polo at the Omah Pala booth.
polo.subtitle: Scan QR codes at the booth, collect stamps, and redeem them for a reward from Omah Pala.
polo.unavailableTitle: Find My Polo isn’t available yet
polo.unavailableBody: This game hasn’t been switched on. Visit the Omah Pala booth for the schedule.
polo.notOpenTitle: Find My Polo hasn’t opened yet
polo.notOpenBody: This event hasn’t started or has already ended. Check again at the Omah Pala booth.
polo.closedBanner: The event isn’t running right now. Your progress is saved, but QR codes can’t be scanned.
polo.step1Title: Sign up and verify your email
polo.step1Body: Create an account with an email and password, then open the verification link we send you.
polo.step2Body: Each account gets 4 target QR codes out of the 10 at the booth. Your targets don’t change during the event.
polo.step3Title: Scan QR codes at the booth
polo.step3Body: A target QR gives one stamp. Any other QR gives no stamp, but opens a product or program page you’ll need to browse for a moment.
polo.step4Body: Two stamps qualify for a small gift. Three stamps unlock a digital sticker. Rewards are redeemed at the booth with a claim code.
